title: night-capacity-signal-cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for a compact internal announcement and Q&A for a temporary night-time capacity signal (low-priority ops mode). Wanted: one-pager we can paste in #all-hands and in the ops incident channel if we need to throttle non-critical jobs overnight.

Key signal (one-liner to share):
We expect reduced inference throughput in region eu-west-1 overnight (00:00–06:00 UTC) for planned capacity rebalancing. Production APIs remain online; non-essential batch jobs may be delayed.

What to include in the message (order):
- Headline (above)
- Why: short reason — capacity rebalancing + hardware firmware patch rollout; low user traffic window chosen
- Scope: region(s) affected, service classes (hosted API, dedicated pools flagged for maintenance), expected window
- Impact: latency increase (5–15% p95), throughput caps on background batch jobs, no data loss expected
- Action for teams: avoid large scheduled evals during the window; postpone bulk embedding backfills; set retry windows; alert SRE if any critical SLAs break
- Escalation: pager -> SRE oncall; second contact Rowan Lee; exec contact Meera Patel for customer comms

Quick Q&A to paste into thread:
Q: Will customer API keys be affected?
A: No — keys remain valid. Rate limiting for background tasks may be tightened. Public latency SLOs are unchanged; internal throughput may be reduced.

Q: Should product teams stop canary rollouts?
A: Prefer pausing non-essential canaries that rely on guaranteed throughput. Small test traffic ok.

Q: Do Dedicated customers need notice?
A: We will surface a short email to Dedicated customers who have pinned capacity in eu-west-1; ops CS will send a templated note (see linked_artifacts).

Ops checklist (pre-send, 30–60m before):
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window with infra (ticket JIRA-OPS-4821)
- [ ] Lock automated scaling rules to avoid flapping
- [ ] Pre-warm critical pools we want to keep stable
- [ ] Post a brief note in #ops-oncall and #all-hands 30m prior
- [ ] Prepare rollback script and confirm runbook steps

Post-window follow-up (next morning):
- Quick metrics snapshot (latency, error-rate, queued jobs) to paste into the thread
- Confirm any customer impact and open follow-ups

Notes to self (draft tone & phrasing):
Hey team — small heads up: we’ll run a brief capacity rebalancing in eu-west-1 on Nov 6 at 00:00–06:00 UTC to finish the firmware rollouts and rebalance batch queue weights. You should see small, temporary throttling of background work only. If you have critical runs scheduled, move them outside that window. Will post a short update before we start and a recap in the morning. Ping Rowan or Meera if you want a 1:1 heads up to your team.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to attach an excerpt of the runbook as copy-paste? (yes, maybe a minimal step list)
- Who will email Dedicated customers (ops-cs or account team)? Confirm template and sender
- Final phrasing for public slack message (keep it calm, no panic)

Draft slack post (short):
"Heads up: planned capacity rebalancing in eu-west-1 tonight 00:00–06:00 UTC. APIs stay online; background jobs may be delayed. We’ll post updates in #ops-oncall and share a morning recap. Contact @rowan or @meera for urgent questions."

Scratch lines / bits to reuse:
- "APIs stay online; background jobs may be delayed."
- "No data loss expected; alert SRE if p99 > 2x baseline."
- "We will share a morning metrics snapshot."

End.
